chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Safwan from Rifa'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife until she became irrevocably divorced from him and her waiting period ended, then she married another husband, so he divorced her as well, then her first husband married her again. Does that demolish the first divorce? He said: Yes.
ai.seo_question: Does a second marriage and subsequent divorce nullify the first irrevocable divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of 'Tahliyah' (or 'Tasbiyah'), where a third divorce is required to make the initial divorce irrevocable. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that if the wife marries another man and he divorces her, the first husband's initial divorce is 'demolished' (haddama), allowing her to return to him under the same original marriage contract without a new mahr or contract. This ruling is pivotal in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between revocable (raj'i) and irrevocable (ba'in) divorces, ensuring the first husband can remarry his ex-wife without the restrictions of a new marriage ceremony.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad and Safwan, from Rafa’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who divorces his wife until she becomes irrevocably divorced from him, and fulfils her waiting period. Then she marries another husband, so he divorces her as well. Then she marries her first husband. Does that demolish the first divorce?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 3. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from Sama‘ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Safwan from Rifa‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his wife and she becomes a stranger to him because of the expiration of her waiting period; then another man marries her who divorces her also; then she marries the first husband; if it destroys the first divorce. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it destroys the first divorce.’ Ibn Sama‘ah has said that ibn Bukayr would say, ‘If a divorced woman is divorced by her husband, then leaves her until she becomes stranger to him, then marries her, she then can live with him on the basis of a new divorce. Ibn Sama‘ah has said that al-Husayn ibn Hashim has mentioned that he asked ibn Bukayr who gave this answer and he then asked, ‘Have you heard anything about it?’ He replied, ‘No, it is what Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has granted in the form of opinion.’ Ibn Sama‘ah has said, ‘We do not accept the words of ibn Bukayr; in fact Hadith says, ‘If there is a husband between them.’”
